_source: NPC/place entries reworded from the offline ER guide (eldenring.wiki.gg CC BY-SA + Fextralife) and this site's own quests.json. Boss entries compressed from data/bosses.json. Route facts only — spoiler-light, matching the guides tab pattern. `chapters` cross-references found by grepping tales/content/ for each entry's name.

entries.name: Ranni the Witch
entries.text: A witch who rules from Ranni's Rise above Caria Manor in Liurnia. Her questline is the game's longest and most rewarding, threading through Nokron, Ainsel River, and the Moonlight Altar. Completing it grants the Dark Moon Greatsword and decides one of the game's endings.

entries.name: Blaidd the Half-Wolf
entries.text: Ranni's sworn wolf-knight, first met howling at Mistwood Ruins in Limgrave. His own quest runs alongside Ranni's and ends, eventually, in a fight you can't avoid. Beating him yields the Royal Greatsword and his armor set.

entries.name: Roderika
entries.text: Found sitting outside Stormhill Shack before Margit, in low spirits. A short questline about the Chrysalids' Memento in Stormveil Castle brings her to Roundtable Hold, where she becomes the Spirit Tuner — the NPC who upgrades your Spirit Ashes for the rest of the game.

entries.name: Sorcerer Rogier
entries.text: A scholar-knight met in Stormveil Castle's chapel, also available as a gold summon against Margit or Godrick. His investigation into Ranni and a hidden corpse beneath the castle threads into Fia's own questline before he meets his end at the Hold.

entries.name: Fia, the Deathbed Companion
entries.text: Offers a comforting hug at Roundtable Hold — accepting it has a cost, which she lifts later. Her questline opens the hidden region of Deeproot Depths and a dragon fight, and completing it unlocks one of the game's endings.

entries.name: D, Hunter of the Dead
entries.text: A masked hunter of the undead, met near Summonwater Village or Roundtable Hold, who opens the way to Gurranq's Bestial Sanctum for Deathroot rewards. His story continues, grimly, through a twin brother later in the game.

entries.name: Brother Corhyn & Goldmask
entries.text: Corhyn, an incantation merchant at Roundtable Hold, serves the silent ascetic Goldmask, the age's great student of the Golden Order's flaws. Their pilgrimage follows you from Altus to Leyndell to the Mountaintops, and finishing it unlocks one of the game's endings.

entries.name: Nepheli Loux
entries.text: A warrior first met as a gold summon against Godrick in Stormveil Castle. Her questline, tied to the dispossessed noble Kenneth Haight, ends with Limgrave finally getting a ruler — and an Arsenal Charm along the way.

entries.name: Dung Eater
entries.text: A cursed prisoner, invisible at Roundtable Hold until you're carrying a Seedbed Curse. Freeing him leads into Leyndell's sewers and unlocks one of the game's endings — or, killed instead, he leaves behind the Sword of Milos.

entries.name: Millicent
entries.text: Millicent, dying of scarlet rot in Caelid's Church of the Plague, is tended by the sage Gowry. Her long recovery pilgrimage runs from Caelid to Altus to the Haligtree itself, and its ending choice affects both her talisman reward and a way to undo the Frenzied Flame.

entries.name: Sorceress Sellen
entries.text: An outlawed sorcerer teaching from Waypoint Ruins' cellar in Limgrave. Her conspiracy against two exiled masters runs through Caelid and Raya Lucaria and rewards sorcery either path you choose, ending at the Grand Library.

entries.name: Tanith & Rya
entries.text: Tanith's Recusants take contracts to hunt down other Tarnished, entered via Rya at Scenic Isle in Liurnia or by walking straight into the manor on Mt. Gelmir. Completing the hunts pays out real weapons and talismans.

entries.name: Patches
entries.text: A recurring trickster first fought in Murkwater Cave, Limgrave — sparing him turns him into a merchant who resurfaces across the whole map, at Volcano Manor and beyond. Worth keeping alive for his shop and hints.

entries.name: Diallos of House Hoslow
entries.text: A knight met at Roundtable Hold, searching for a lost woman named Lanya. His path runs through Volcano Manor's Recusant letters before he settles at Jarburg, a village of living jars in Liurnia, and offers his gear as thanks.

entries.name: White-Mask Varré
entries.text: The masked stranger who greets every Tarnished at The First Step. His invasion-and-knighthood questline through the Rose Church ends with a free teleport straight to the late-game Mohgwyn Palace — a shortcut, not an invitation to fight what's there early.

entries.name: Boc the Seamster
entries.text: A talking bush near Gatefront Ruins in Limgrave turns out to be Boc, a tailor. Free him and equip him properly and he'll alter your armor for free all the way to Leyndell — one of the gentler questlines in the game.

entries.name: Latenna the Albinauric
entries.text: An Albinauric archer found at Slumbering Wolf's Shack in Liurnia, tied to a medallion split in two halves. Reuniting them at the Grand Lift of Rold opens the hidden Consecrated Snowfield region.

entries.name: Yura, Hunter of Bloody Fingers
entries.text: A katana-wielding hunter of invaders met near Agheel Lake in Limgrave. Helping him through a rival's ambush and a later confrontation at the Second Church of Marika earns his Nagakiba early — a katana that holds up all game.

entries.name: Alexander, Iron Fist
entries.text: A warrior jar found stuck in a hole in Limgrave — hit him from behind to free him. His pilgrimage of misadventures across Caelid and Mt. Gelmir ends in a duel at Crumbling Farum Azula, rewarding one of the game's best skill-damage talismans.

entries.name: Hyetta
entries.text: A blind pilgrim met at Lake-Facing Cliffs in Liurnia, feeding on grapes tied to a hidden flame. Her questline leads deep beneath Leyndell and, taken to its end, locks in one of the game's endings — a commitment, not a quick detour.

entries.name: Thops
entries.text: A locked-out sorcery student who opens a shop at the Church of Irith once you donate runes. Bringing him a second Academy Glintstone Key gets him back into Raya Lucaria and unlocks his sorcery and staff.

entries.name: Margit, the Fell Omen
entries.text: The game's first real wall, blocking the road to Stormveil Castle in Limgrave. Weak to Bleed, Frost, and most status effects — bring a Spirit Ash and don't be afraid to level up elsewhere and come back.

entries.name: Godrick the Grafted
entries.text: Stormveil Castle's grafted lord, weak to Magic and Fire and most status effects. His second phase grafts on a dragon's head — stay at his side or behind him, never in front.

entries.name: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
entries.text: The Full Moon Queen, found adrift in Raya Lucaria's Grand Library. Her first phase is a puzzle — kill the three glowing students to drop her shield — and her Great Rune lets you respec your stats afterward.

entries.name: Starscourge Radahn
entries.text: A demigod general fought at a festival in Redmane Castle, Caelid, weak to Scarlet Rot and Sleep. Beating him raises your max HP/FP/Stamina and opens the way to Nokron, Eternal City.

entries.name: Morgott, the Omen King
entries.text: The Omen King, guarding the throne room of Leyndell, the Royal Capital. Weak to Bleed, Frost, and most status effects — the same delayed-swing baits that work on Margit apply here too.

entries.name: Fire Giant
entries.text: A towering boss at Flame Peak in the Mountaintops of the Giants, weak to Frost above all. Stay close and behind him — his second-phase rolling fire wheel needs a perpendicular sprint, not a straight-line race.

entries.name: Godskin Duo
entries.text: Two Godskin fighters in Crumbling Farum Azula who share one health bar — killing one just revives it, so grind the shared bar down. Sleep status is huge here: put one to sleep and gang the other.

entries.name: Maliketh, the Black Blade
entries.text: Marika's shadow-beast, fought in two forms at Crumbling Farum Azula — first as the Beast Clergyman, then as the Black Blade itself. Beating him is this game's world-changing story trigger, so wrap up NPC questlines first.

entries.name: Godfrey, First Elden Lord
entries.text: The first Elden Lord, fought a second time in Leyndell's Capital of Ash. His ground-slam shockwaves want a jump, not a roll, and his second phase adds unblockable grabs with a clear wind-up.

entries.name: Radagon / Elden Beast
entries.text: The base game's two-part final boss, fought back-to-back with no flask refill between them at the Erdtree — pace your healing accordingly. Radagon parries; the Elden Beast wants constant forward sprinting.

entries.name: Mohg, Lord of Blood
entries.text: The Blood Lord, found in his underground palace, reachable via Varré's early shortcut or the Consecrated Snowfield teleporter. Bring a Purifying Crystal Tear physick to blunt his brutal second-phase Nihil ritual.

entries.name: Malenia, Blade of Miquella
entries.text: Widely considered the hardest fight in the base game, found at the root of the Haligtree. She heals on every hit she lands, even blocked ones — don't turtle behind a shield, and watch for Waterfowl Dance.

entries.name: Astel, Naturalborn of the Void
entries.text: A void-born horror at the end of Ranni's questline, past the Lake of Rot. Free camera tracks its teleports and meteor barrage better than a locked one — stay near its head, where many attacks miss.

entries.name: Divine Beast Dancing Lion
entries.text: An early DLC boss at Belurat, Tower Settlement — bring a couple of Scadutree Blessings before trying, since fragments matter more than levels here. It wields lightning, frost, and wind by turns, so don't over-commit to one resistance.

entries.name: Rellana, Twin Moon Knight
entries.text: The DLC's first real skill check, fought at Castle Ensis. Her sword-chains are dodgeable at point-blank but dangerous at mid-range, and her Twin Moons finisher rewards a jump on the third blast, not a roll.

entries.name: Messmer the Impaler
entries.text: Marika's exiled son, guarding Shadow Keep. Most of his combos end in a long recovery worth waiting out, and mid-fight he transforms into a serpent with a sprint-away-then-roll dive attack.

entries.name: Bayle the Dread
entries.text: An optional dragon fight atop Jagged Peak, capping off a pilgrimage that's worth doing for its own sake. Fight from under his left side, where his head slams and breath mostly miss.

entries.name: Midra, Lord of Frenzied Flame
entries.text: A hidden DLC boss deep in the Abyssal Woods — getting there safely (crouch-walking past the Aged Ones) is half the challenge. In the arena itself, every flame flurry has a clean pause worth punishing.

entries.name: Romina, Saint of the Bud
entries.text: A rot-saint guarding the Church of the Bud on the road to the DLC's finale. She's a mobility fight — sprint under her centipede vault landing rather than backing away, and punish after her rot bloom.

entries.name: Promised Consort Radahn
entries.text: The DLC's final boss, at Enir-Ilim — widely regarded as one of FromSoftware's hardest fights. Bring Scadutree Blessing 18–20 at minimum; losing repeatedly here is the intended experience, not a sign to give up.

entries.name: Rykard, Lord of Blasphemy
entries.text: Volcano Manor's serpent-fused lord. Grab the Serpent-Hunter spear at the arena entrance before the fight — normal weapons barely scratch him, and his skull-rain is easily interrupted by the spear's own skill.

entries.name: Limgrave
entries.text: The starting region — storm-battered coastline, ruined forts, and Stormveil Castle guarding the way north. Most players' first dozen or so hours happen here, and it holds an unusually dense cluster of early NPC questlines.

entries.name: Weeping Peninsula
entries.text: A small optional region south of Limgrave, reachable early via a bridge or a fall from the cliffs above. Worth a detour before Stormveil for the levels, and it's where Irina's fate quietly gates Hyetta's later questline.

entries.name: Liurnia
entries.text: A flooded lake region north of Limgrave, home to Raya Lucaria Academy and the Carian royal family's ruins. Enemies here hit harder than Limgrave's — expect a difficulty step up once you cross the cliffs.

entries.name: Caelid
entries.text: A scarlet-rot wasteland east of Liurnia, one of the most dangerous early-accessible regions in the game. Rot buildup is the real threat here more than raw damage — carry Preserving Boluses or immunizing gear.

entries.name: Altus Plateau
entries.text: A golden highland reached via the Grand Lift of Dectus or a hidden Waygate, marking the game's rough halfway point. Enemy difficulty jumps noticeably here, and it's the gateway to Leyndell.

entries.name: Mt. Gelmir / Volcano Manor
entries.text: A volcanic region west of Altus, home to Volcano Manor and its Recusant assassination contracts. The climb up is lava-and-cliffside dangerous; the manor itself hides a much stranger threat beneath its parlors.

entries.name: Leyndell
entries.text: The golden Royal Capital, seat of the Erdtree and the game's major mid-to-late story turning point. It's visited twice across the story, in two very different states — the second visit is best not spoiled in advance.

entries.name: Mountaintops
entries.text: A frozen late-game region reached via the Grand Lift of Rold, home to the Fire Giants' old territory and Castle Sol. Cold, sparse, and a good sign you're entering the endgame stretch.

entries.name: Consecrated Snowfield
entries.text: A hidden snowfield past the Mountaintops, accessible only with both halves of a medallion from Latenna's questline. A featureless blizzard hides one of the game's more elaborate optional dungeons underneath.

entries.name: Haligtree
entries.text: Miquella's tree, raised as a refuge for the Erdtree's outcasts, reached through the Consecrated Snowfield. One of the most punishing optional areas in the game, guarding the fight many consider hardest in the base game.

entries.name: Underground (Nokron, Nokstella, Siofra, Deeproot)
entries.text: A cluster of ancient sunken cities beneath the surface — Nokron, Nokstella, Siofra River, and Deeproot Depths — each lit by false stars instead of a sky. Access to most of them opens only after specific story triggers, not by simply walking in.

entries.name: Roundtable Hold
entries.text: The Tarnished's home base, outside the normal map, reached via Melina after the first Site of Grace. Most major NPC questlines pass through here at some point — check back after every region boss.

entries.name: Land of Shadow
entries.text: The Shadow of the Erdtree expansion's entire map — a hidden realm accessed through Mohg's remembrance after defeating him. Its own difficulty curve runs steeper than the base game, gated by Scadutree Blessing fragments rather than character level.
